stories.title: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
stories.explanation: OpenAI has been valued at $1.25 trillion in a new $11 billion funding round, making it one of the world's most valuable companies. This news follows Anthropic's IPO filing and indicates continued significant investment in OpenAI.

stories.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
stories.explanation: The US government is reportedly approving sales of NVIDIA's AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies, including one with an empty office. Concerns are being raised about due diligence in vetting these firms for handling advanced AI chips.

stories.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
stories.explanation: A new report indicates Anthropic is using AI to accelerate its own AI research, with models improving twice as quickly as a year ago. This development is alarming researchers given Anthropic's public calls for slowing down AI development.

stories.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
stories.explanation: OpenAI is partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in its systems, focusing on interactions with third-party services. This initiative aims to strengthen OpenAI's defenses and accelerate cyber defense with frontier AI.

stories.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
stories.explanation: Crusoe sold its unfinished Wyoming data center project to Google, which plans to invest $17 billion to develop the campus. This deal highlights the challenges independent developers face in delivering massive AI data center projects on time and within budget.

stories.title: China reportedly recruited AI exec to spy on Jensen Huang
stories.explanation: China's intelligence agency reportedly recruited businesswoman Alice Huang to spy on NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang for information on American AI chips. The aim was to glean intelligence and potentially influence NVIDIA to make advanced chips available to China.

stories.title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
stories.explanation: New research shows that free Chinese AI models like DeepSeek and GLM are becoming nearly as capable at hacking simulated networks as advanced closed models. This suggests open-weight models are matching frontier models in cyber skills, potentially making efforts to limit access to advanced AI less effective.

stories.title: AI Companies Really, Really Want to Buy Your Work Files and Emails
stories.explanation: AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly paying significant sums to data brokers for internal corporate files and emails to train their AI models, indicating a growing demand for private data.

stories.title: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
stories.explanation: Hugging Face introduced ToyBlocks, a framework for creating controlled simulated environments called FoundationWorlds for robot learning and evaluation. This allows researchers to study robot behavior and model improvement more effectively.

stories.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
stories.explanation: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the Chinese-made AI hacking tool Artex publicly exposed to the internet. This open-source autonomous penetration testing tool, linked to cyberattacks, allows anyone to access it and potentially launch cyberattacks.
